To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the assembly reaction products (i.e., normal capsid, non-capsid polymer, intermediaries, and free dimesic core protein) of HBV were quantified in response to three experimental assembly effectors, and the thermodynamic and kinetic effects of assembly effectors, not aberrant capsid formation, correlate with maximal activity against HBV.
Assembly effectors are antiviral compounds that induce aberrant capsid assembly, but the mechanism of antiviral action is not through this effect.
assembly reaction products were quantified in order to identify attributes of hepatitis virus (HBV).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of small molecules that can be used to treat hepatitis B infection.
the design, synthesis and evaluation of small-molecule antivirals that target the assembly of the hepatitis B virus capsid.
identifying the attributes of assembly effectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the assembly effectors HAP12, AT-130, and HAP13 are not assembly effectors but rather bind capsid proteins and block capsid formation by a variety of mechanisms.
the antiviral activity of these compounds is not due to aberrant assembly but to thermodynamic and kinetic effects.
the antiviral activity of assembly effectors is a consequence of their ability to inhibit capsid assembly by binding to polymer intermediates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phase diagrams map the properties of the antiviral agents directed against HBV core assembly.
the antiviral activity of an assembly effector is a function of the binding constant, the binding stoichiometry, and the effect on the thermodynamic or kinetic parameters of the assembly reaction.
HBV assembly effectors can be divided into three categories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the assembly effectors we have identified are not antiviral through a mechanism of inhibiting capsid assembly.
antiviral activity is not a consequence of aberrant capsid assembly.
the antiviral activity of assembly effectors is not a function of their ability to inhibit capsid assembly, but rather their ability to bind and inhibit the assembly of the capsid protein.
